tour.overview:
Coimbra, the medieval capital of Portugal, is home to one of the oldest universities in the world, founded in 1290 and settled in the royal palace on the hilltop in 1537. Its Joanina Library, a baroque treasure of gilded wood, and its student traditions, including black capes and Coimbra fado, have made the university a UNESCO World Heritage Site. On the coast nearby, Aveiro is a town of canals and colourful moliceiro boats.

This private day combines both with a licensed guide and a vehicle, starting from Porto or Lisbon.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours from Porto, 11 hours from Lisbon
• Start and end: your hotel in Porto or Lisbon
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, vehicle and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; steep streets in Coimbra

WHAT YOU SEE
• The University of Coimbra and the Joanina Library.
• The old cathedral.
• Aveiro’s canals.
• Costa Nova.

WHY THIS WORKS
Coimbra and Aveiro sit between Porto and Lisbon; a private vehicle combines them easily, and can even link the two cities.

WHO IT SUITS
History lovers, families and travellers moving between Porto and Lisbon.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
This tour can be done one-way between Porto and Lisbon on request.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The Joanina Library has timed entry with limited capacity; photography inside is not allowed.

days.name: The University of Coimbra, the Joanina Library, the old town, and the canals of Aveiro
days.description:
What to expect: Coimbra’s university and Aveiro’s canals, with a licensed guide, private vehicle, tickets, boat ride and tasting.

Your guide and driver collect you in the morning and drive to Coimbra. At the university, on the hilltop, you cross the Paço das Escolas courtyard, see the ceremonial Sala dos Capelos where doctoral degrees are awarded, the Chapel of São Miguel with its baroque organ, and the Joanina Library, built in the 1720s, with gilded and lacquered shelves holding some 60,000 books, protected by a colony of bats that eat the insects at night.

You walk down through the medieval upper town to the Romanesque old cathedral and the student 'republics', and your guide explains the traditions of the capes and the serenades of Coimbra fado. After lunch (not included), you drive to Aveiro, where you ride a moliceiro boat, painted with colourful and sometimes cheeky scenes, along the canals lined with Art Nouveau houses. You taste ovos moles, egg-yolk sweets in wafer shells shaped like seashells, and end at Costa Nova, with its rows of red-, blue- and green-striped wooden houses facing the lagoon.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Pick-up in Porto (or 07:30 in Lisbon).
10:00 – University of Coimbra.
12:00 – Upper town and old cathedral.
13:00 – Lunch break.
14:45 – Aveiro and the moliceiro boat.
16:00 – Ovos moles tasting.
16:45 – Costa Nova.
18:30 – Back in Porto.

GOOD TO KNOW
• A one-way tour between Porto and Lisbon can be arranged with your luggage.
• A Coimbra fado concert can be added in the evening on a 2-day version.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, licensed guide, university ticket, boat ride, tasting, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Can we start in Lisbon?
faq.answer: Yes. The day is longer, about 11 hours, or it can be done one-way.

faq.question: Can we take photos in the Joanina Library?
faq.answer: No, photography is not allowed inside.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: No. Your guide suggests a restaurant serving chanfana or leitão (suckling pig) nearby.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children enjoy the boat and the striped houses.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Coimbra is very steep; the vehicle can take you up to the university.

faq.question: Is the boat private?
faq.answer: Standard moliceiro rides are shared; a private boat can be arranged.

faq.question: Can we hear Coimbra fado?
faq.answer: Yes, at an evening concert, on a 2-day version.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year; May brings the student festival, the Queima das Fitas.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not obligatory in Portugal, but rounding up or leaving 5 to 10 percent for a guide or driver you were happy with is appreciated.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
